source.title: Mini-review: Prediction errors, attention and associative learning

confidence_rationale: Authoritative review of the Pearce-Hall associability literature by the lab that produced most of the CeA circuit data. Directly states the Rescorla-Wagner vs Pearce-Hall split that MECH-598 rests on (PE changes US effectiveness vs PE changes CS associability). Confidence held at 0.60 because the reviewed evidence is overwhelmingly APPETITIVE and OMISSION-driven, while MECH-598 is triggered by an unexpected aversive DELIVERY.
failure_signatures: The reviewed associability enhancements are induced almost entirely by the surprising OMISSION of an expected food outcome; an aversive-delivery trigger is not what this literature measured.
The review describes associability changes for USs as well as CSs, so a per-CANDIDATE-CAUSE learning-rate state is only one of the loci at which PE can alter event processing.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Prediction error acts in two ways: as the Rescorla-Wagner effectiveness of the reinforcer, and as the Pearce-Hall associability of the conditioned stimuli present when PE occurred, so that those cues enter new learning faster later. PE-induced associability changes involve widespread brain systems for coding, storage and retrieval.
mapping.ree_translation: MECH-598 is the Pearce-Hall half: an aversive PE raises the future learning rate of candidate causes present in a retrospective window, as a persistent per-candidate state. The review is the canonical statement that this is a behaviourally separable operation from a delta rule, which is the half an E3 harm regression readout already implements.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Valence and sign mismatch: the lab's paradigms are appetitive (food) and mostly omission-induced. The review supports the computational form of MECH-598, not its aversive trigger. It is also a single-lab synthesis.
mapping.source_context: Rat Pavlovian serial-prediction and unblocking paradigms; lesion and inactivation; review

confidence_components.notes: Source quality good (focused review, primary data behind it are replicated within-lab). Mapping to the computational form is high, to the aversive trigger low; averaged 0.62. Transfer risk moderate: rodent appetitive to an abstract agent's aversive channel.
